items.text: Concept 3 · Summation

items.quote: Use the summation symbol to represent mathematical sequences
items.text: Learning Outcomes: Use the summation symbol to represent mathematical sequences and calculate their values in different sequences.

items.quote: In environmental biology, forest recovery follows a dual-force mathematical pattern.
items.text: Forest recovery example: after a wildfire conservationists plant 200 saplings, adding 100 more each year (arithmetic progression 200, 300, 400...), while only 60% of trees survive from one year to the next (geometric decay, ratio 0.6). Calculating the total surviving population after a decade needs tracking how each year's planting cycle decays; summation notation gives a unified framework to analyze linear growth and exponential decay.

items.quote: is the sum from the first term to the n−th term of a geometric
items.claim: The sum of a r^{k-1} for k from 1 to n is the sum from the first term to the n-th term of a geometric sequence with first term a and common ratio r.

items.quote: When r < 1, Σ ar^{k-1} = a(1 − r^n)/(1 − r)
items.claim: When r<1 the sum of the first n terms equals a(1-r^n)/(1-r).
When r>1 the sum of the first n terms equals a(r^n-1)/(r-1).

items.quote: A sequence expressed as a_n = r^{n−1} can be rewritten as
items.claim: A sequence a_n = r^{n-1} can be rewritten as a_n = 1 × r^{n-1}, so it is a geometric sequence with first term 1 and common ratio r. Example: a_n = 4^{n-1} = 1 × 4^{n-1}; first term 1, common ratio 4.

items.quote: A sequence expressed as a_n = r^n can be rewritten as
items.claim: A sequence a_n = r^n can be rewritten as a_n = r × r^{n-1}, so it is a geometric sequence with first term r and common ratio r. Example: a_n = 4^n = 4 × 4^{n-1}; first term 4, common ratio 4.

items.text: Find the following sum S
Explanation

items.quote: The sum to be found is the sum of (Arithmetic sequence with first term 3
items.text: The sum to be found is the sum of (Arithmetic sequence with first term 3, the common difference 2) × (Geometric sequence with the first term 1, the common ratio 3). Then S = 3×1+5×3+7×3²+9×3³+…+(2n+1)×3^{n−1}. Multiply both sides by the common ratio 3 of the geometric sequence: 3S = 3×3+5×3²+7×3³+9×3⁴+…+(2n+1)×3^n. Subtract the sides of the two equations: S−3S gives −2S = 3×1+2×3+2×3²+2×3³+…+2×3^{n−1} −(2n+1)×3^n; then −2S = 3 + 2(3^n−1)/(3−1) −2 −(2n+1)×3^n; −2S = 3^n −(2n+1)×3^n; −2S = −2n×3^n; S = n×3^n.

Side notes beside the explanation: 'Use S − rS.'; 'Write the equations so that the powers of the common ratio align vertically.'; 'Supplement terms to make subtraction easier.'; 'The sum from the 2nd term to the n-th term of a geometric sequence with first term 2, common ratio 3. (The sum from the first term to the n-th term The first term)'; 'Divide both sides by -2 Watch the '-' sign.'

items.quote: If a_n found by S_n − S_{n−1} is a_n= 2n²−2n+1
items.stem: If $a_n$ found by $S_n - S_{n-1}$ is $a_n = 2n^2-2n+1$ ...(i), and $a_1$ found from $S_1$ is $a_1=0$ ...(ii), substituting $n=1$ into (i) gives $a_1=1$, which does not hold.
solution: Substituting $n=1$ into (i) gives $a_1=1$, which does not hold (differs from $a_1=0$).
Therefore, the general term is $a_1=0$, and $a_n = 2n^2-2n+1$ when $n\ge2$.
